incidents.classification: Actual build artifact drift caught before deployment; not an ECS outage
incidents.phase: Local image build and artifact acceptance
incidents.symptom: Original Dockerfile build exited 0, but artifact comparison reported BLOCKED_ARTIFACT_DIFFERENCE: certifi changed from 2026.10.18 to 2026.10.19.
incidents.direct_cause: Package installation resolved a newer transitive certifi version during the application image build.
incidents.root_cause: The original build did not preserve all deployed transitive dependency versions; build success alone did not establish dependency identity.
incidents.failed_attempt: The initial docker build completed successfully (exit 0, 70.363 seconds) and its image verification subprocess also exited 0, while the verification status correctly blocked artifact acceptance. The first image was not deployed and was retained under the -dependency-drift tag.
incidents.verified_fix: A build-only Dockerfile layered FROM the retained drift image and ran RUN pip install --no-cache-dir --no-deps certifi==2026.10.18. Rebuild exited 0 (5.662 seconds); stable verification reported LOCAL_VERIFIED, empty dependency_differences, source_manifest_matches=true. Repository requirements were not modified.
incidents.recognition_condition: Compare actual image package versions to the old deployed package manifest and inspect semantic verification status even when process exit_code=0; non-empty dependency_differences blocks transfer/cutover.
incidents.prevention: For application-only updates, retain old dependency identity evidence, diff the full actual package manifest before transfer, and explicitly block any unexplained drift. Preserve the first failed artifact and result; do not overwrite evidence with a passing rebuild.

incidents.classification: Actual read-only preflight acceptance error; not data loss or deployment-induced database failure
incidents.symptom: remote_data_before.py exited 2 with REVIEW_REQUIRED; physical_documents, physical_chunks, physical_vectors, and prepared_ready_documents checks were false while physical prepared-pool totals, read-only isolation, scope, and indexes passed.
incidents.direct_cause: The check compared post-alignment database state to older physical-count and prepared-ready reference values.
incidents.root_cause: Historical frozen prepared-pool identity and current enabled versions were treated as interchangeable. Prior source alignment added 28 documents/657 vectors and disabled 52 old versions/474 vectors without deleting payloads; 27 disabled documents/355 vectors belonged to the original prepared pool.
incidents.failed_attempt: The initial historical-reference probe returned REVIEW_REQUIRED and was preserved. It was not rewritten to PASS or presented as an application outage.
incidents.verified_fix: Local ID/version evidence reconciliation explained 11708+28=11736 documents, 28000+657=28657 vectors, and prepared_ready=11683-27=11656. D8 acceptance then compared its actual frozen pre-cutover snapshot with the post-cutover snapshot; all 14 data protection checks passed. Reconciliation itself made no remote query; optional exact-ID SQL remained NOT_RUN.
incidents.recognition_condition: When preflight count checks fail after approved source-version replacement, compare physical rows, historical prepared-pool membership, and enabled/current versions separately. Check exact mapped replacement IDs and preserved prior evidence before attributing the mismatch to the new deployment.
incidents.prevention: Version data baselines with source-alignment provenance. Freeze a current read-only before snapshot for same-release before/after protection and retain original failed receipts. Do not silently alter old thresholds or call physical retention proof of old-version enablement.
